items.content:
Oh My Hermes workflows now work outside Hermes.

If you spend your day in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, OpenClaw or pi, you can install the same 121 OMH workflows as Agent Skills and call them from the agent you already use. That includes code review, ulw-plan, ulw-research and incident response, plus the rest of the catalog.

Setup is one clone and one script per host. The installer is plain shell (PowerShell on Windows), so you don't need Python or the omh CLI to install it.

git clone https://t.co/A6JSJceYUP ~/oh-my-hermes
sh ~/oh-my-hermes/.cursor/install.sh

Swap .cursor for .claude, .codex, .opencode, .openclaw or .pi.

Inside Hermes you still get the routing, memory and TUI on top. Outside it, the workflows come with you.

https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E

items.summary: Teknium reports that a traced issue was unrelated to the user's problem or was broken in 0.22.5 with a fix coming in the 0.22.6 patch release tomorrow, and shares Hermes' own analysis explaining that issue #143869's cause does not occur in a running Hermes, leading to PR #143872 being closed while the Discord-reported missed-wake issue stays open.
items.reasoning: Rich technical detail: mentions specific issue and PR numbers, the closed PR #143872, gateway subagent ownership internals, and an imminent 0.22.6 patch. High-value debugging insight from the lead dev despite low engagement.
items.summary_html: Teknium reports that a traced issue was unrelated to the user's problem or was broken in 0.22.5 with a fix coming in the 0.22.6 patch release tomorrow, and shares Hermes' own analysis explaining that issue #143869's cause does not occur in a running Hermes, leading to PR #143872 being closed while the Discord-reported missed-wake issue stays open.
items.content_html:
@danonino_rmz I think the issue is just simply not related to your problem, or it was broken on 0.22.5 and will be fixed when the patch release for 0.22.6 comes out tomorrow;

my hermes said:

The cause described in #143869 doesn't happen in a running Hermes, so there was nothing to fix in code. I closed the PR that tried to fix it, #143872. The issue stays open, because the Discord reporter's missed wake is real but still unexplained.

Why the described cause doesn't happen: a background subagent started from a gateway chat (Discord, Telegram and so on) always has no execution owner recorded. When it finishes, the gateway picks the result up through a check that never looks at that owner field. The ownership check the issue blames only applies to separate worker processes, and those never pick up rows written by another process. The bug only shows up in the PR's test, which inserts such a row by hand and then calls the worker's handlers on it.
